newsitem.title: USA: NYC agency approves lease of Coney Island hospital.
newsitem.headline: NYC agency approves lease of Coney Island hospital.

text.p: New York City's Health and Hospitals Corp on Friday, in a major step for the Giuliani Administration's privatizing effort, approved a pact to lease the city's first public hospital to a for-profit company.

Under the agreement, PHS NY, a unit of PHS Inc, which runs health care companies in Cleveland and Philadelphia, would sublet the Coney Island Hospital in Brooklyn for 99 years. The company agreed to pay the Health and Hospitals Corp $42.1 million for most of the $49 million of outstanding debt.

City sources, who declined to be named, speculated that it might take a number of months for the Giuliani Administration to get the state to approve the pact and there are several lawsuits that are trying to block the deal from going ahead.
The state Health Department said that it has yet to get the city's application, and thus cannot say how long it might take for it to act.

Asked about the state's policy towards privatization, a spokesman for the department said that some smaller hospitals now are being leased, though he noted the periods are much shorter than in the city's new pact.
"There are management contracts in existence, mostly at rural hospitals upstate, for managing hospitals, and by regulation, we limit them to three years," said Bob Hinckley.

And if the deal, which has been blasted by the city comptroller, Alan Hevesi, looks likely to close, the New York City Council is poised to block it in court. "The City Council, in our lawsuit, will move for a preliminary injunction to prevent the closing," said Richard Weinberg, the council's counsel.

He explained that this step would only be taken if there is a need for urgent action. Otherwise, the Council will wait for Judge Herbert Posner of the Supreme Court of New York, Queens County, to rule on the lawsuit it brought against the Giuliani Administration.

The council argues that it must be involved in the sale of any city hospital under the land use statutes and because it inherited the powers exercized by the Board of Estimates until it was abolished in 1990.
Both the Giuliani Administration and the City Council have asked for a summary judgment in their favor, and Judge Posner is expected to issue his decision in January.
The board of the New York City Health and Hospitals Corp approved the lease to PHS NY by a margin of 10 to three, said Steve Osborne, a spokesman for the agency said.

Two of the three board members who voted against the plan have sued the Health and Hospitals Corp to block the deal, though they have agreed to drop a move for a temporary restraining order. They instead agreed to review the contract 48 hours before it is signed.
Another lawsuit that is pending was brought by The Campaign to Save Our Public Hospitals, a private coalition.
The city comptroller, who has scathingly criticized the proposed deal, on Friday accused the Giuliani Adminsitration of hiding vital information about the agreement.
In written remarks, he added that that the Health and Hospitals Corp was selling a public hospital without asking the most basic questions about care and cost.

Vowing to continue to serve the taxpayers and the residents of southern Brooklyn by continuing to investigate the pact, he reiterated his skepticism that the city would realize the savings it has estimated.
New York City has said it expects the pact to save it $100 million immediately, and $30 million each year.
